judgments.forked_readings_summary:
All four readings describe the SAME task: port the single AccountLookup read endpoint GET /account/{ani} and its CustomerInfoRepository (calling stored proc cpsl_getAccount_v2) from .NET Framework 4.8 to .NET 10, preserving the exact wire contract (AccountResponse {accountId, status, balance}, camelCase), result codes (E0001 auth-fail, W0011 empty ANI), and the existing channel-gate header auth unchanged — explicitly excluding partner endpoints.

SCOPE: Full agreement. All four center on one endpoint + one repository + one stored proc, one PR/one service, partner endpoints explicitly out. All four name the same identifiers byte-for-byte (cpsl_getAccount_v2, E0001, W0011, the three fields).

SURFACES: Full agreement on the load-bearing surfaces — controller/endpoint, data-access (CustomerInfoRepository + proc), wire/serialization (camelCase, 3-field DTO), result-code envelope, channel-gate auth, host/DI/config bootstrap. All five surfaces map cleanly across readings.

BEHAVIOR: Full agreement on the externally-observable contract — exact field set, camelCase, identical E0001/W0011 strings and triggers, unchanged auth semantics, verbatim proc/param names, framework-port-not-feature-change.

The variations are differences in DETAIL/EMPHASIS, not task, and all are framework-consistent (the repo's 'preserve exactly' / verbatim-DB-identifier discipline):
1. Process framing depth: Readings 1 and 2 foreground the preflight migration-skill pipeline heavily (Phase 1 discovery deliverables — dependency-map.json, behavior-spec.json, legacy-db-name-contract, extraction SQL; WIRE-B golden tied to real DI serializer options; per-service CI workflow accountlookup-pull-request.yaml; vendored parity-check.sh/spec-integrity-check.sh; coverage floor 85%; fix-and-close handoff). Readings 3 and 4 focus on the concrete code-level port and mention testing/spec more lightly. This is the same job at different altitudes — the migrate skill prescribes that pipeline regardless, so it is implied in all four.
2. Implementation-tactic specifics that go slightly beyond what's stated: Reading 4 asserts async-end-to-end ADO.NET/Dapper with CancellationToken (no sync ExecuteReader) and specific .NET-Framework-infra swaps (ConfigurationManager→IOptions, Unity→MS.DI, web.config→appsettings); Reading 3 names Microsoft.Data.SqlClient replacing System.Data.SqlClient. These are reasonable modernization tactics inside the same port, not scope changes.
3. Target DB engine assumption splits but is harmless: Readings 1 and 2 assume Postgres/Aurora as the migrated target (proc/param NAMES stay legacy-exact); Readings 3 and 4 assume SQL Server stays. All four agree the proc name and parameters are preserved verbatim and the proc itself is not modified, so the wire/contract behavior is identical regardless — the engine question is explicitly flagged as an assumption by each.

These are minor variations that do not change which task is being done, which surfaces are touched, or the observable behavior. Net divergence is low.

All four readings describe the SAME task: port the single AccountLookup IVR read endpoint GET /account/{ani} and its CustomerInfoRepository (stored proc cpsl_getAccount_v2) from .NET Framework 4.8 to .NET 10, preserving the exact wire contract (AccountResponse {accountId, status, balance} camelCase), the two result codes (E0001 auth-fail, W0011 empty ANI), and the existing channel-gate header auth unchanged, while explicitly leaving partner endpoints behind. Agreement is total on scope boundary (one endpoint + its repository, one PR, partner endpoints out), on the load-bearing surfaces (controller, data-access/stored-proc, wire-format/serialization, auth, host/DI bootstrap), and on every key behavior (exact field set, camelCase, identical result-code strings + trigger conditions, byte-exact proc/param names, identical auth semantics, framework-port-not-feature-change). All four independently name the same concrete artifacts (CTI.MicroService.IVR.AccountLookup, cpsl_getAccount_v2, E0001/W0011, channel-gate header) and the same exclusion (partner endpoints).

The only differences are minor and non-material:
1) Framework-process framing: readings #1 and #2 emphasize the full preflight migration pipeline (Phase 1 discovery deliverables — dependency-map.json, behavior-spec.json baseline, legacy-db-name-contract.md, extraction SQL; WIRE-B/wire-golden tests wired to real DI JsonSerializerOptions; per-service CI workflow accountlookup-pull-request.yaml; vendored parity-check.sh/spec-integrity-check.sh; 85% coverage floor; handoff to fix-and-close for Stage 1/Stage 2). Readings #3 and #4 focus on the code-level port itself and mention testing/spec compliance more lightly. This is a difference in altitude/emphasis (how much of the surrounding preflight ceremony each spelled out), not a different task — #3 and #4 still acknowledge the generation spec governs patterns and that discovery precedes generation.
2) Data-access mechanism specifics: #3 assumes Microsoft.Data.SqlClient (ADO.NET, no EF); #4 adds async-end-to-end + CancellationToken + possibly Dapper and explicit infra swaps (ConfigurationManager→IOptions, Unity→MS.DI, web.config→appsettings); #1/#2 stay engine-agnostic and even raise PostgreSQL/Aurora as the possible modern target while keeping proc/param names legacy-exact. This is a genuine but minor surface variation about HOW the modernized data layer is wired — none of it changes the observable contract all four agree must be preserved byte-for-byte, and all four agree the proc name/params and the wire shape are immutable.
3) Target DB engine: #1/#2 flag SQL-Server-vs-Postgres as an open assumption; #3/#4 assume SQL Server stays. All four agree this does not affect the in-scope work because identifier names stay legacy-exact and schema authority lives in the legacy DB. This is an assumption gap, not a scope fork.

Net: full agreement on scope, behavior, and the externally-observable contract; only minor variation in which internal-modernization surfaces and pipeline steps each engineer chose to enumerate.

All four read the SAME task: port the single AccountLookup GET /account/{ani} endpoint and its CustomerInfoRepository (stored proc cpsl_getAccount_v2) from .NET Framework 4.8 to .NET 10, preserving byte-exact wire contract (camelCase AccountResponse {accountId, status, balance}), result codes E0001 (auth fail) / W0011 (empty ANI), and the channel-gate header auth unchanged — with partner endpoints explicitly excluded. Surfaces are identical across all four (controller/endpoint, data-access + proc call, wire/serialization, channel-gate auth, host/DI/config). Core behaviors are identical (three-field camelCase output, E0001/W0011 emission conditions, byte-exact proc + param names, no caller-visible change, no proc modification).

The only real variation is scope BREADTH of deliverables, not the task itself: #1 and #2 enumerate the full preflight migration-skill pipeline as in-scope work products (Phase 1 discovery artifacts — dependency-map.json, behavior-spec.json legacy baseline, legacy-db-name-contract.md, extraction SQL; WIRE-B golden tests wired to real DI JsonSerializerOptions; per-service CI workflow accountlookup-pull-request.yaml; vendored parity-check.sh/spec-integrity-check.sh; 85% coverage floor; handoff to fix-and-close for Stage 1 review + Stage 2 Copilot PR loop). #3 and #4 frame the job primarily as the .NET code port and treat the framework's discovery/parity/CI scaffolding as governing context rather than enumerating it — though #3 explicitly notes 'this is a migration-skill job: Phase 1 discovery precedes Phase 2' and #4 cites following the repo's generation spec and migration rubric §M, so they do not contradict the pipeline, they just under-specify it.

A secondary, smaller variation: #4 mandates async-everywhere ADO.NET/Dapper with CancellationToken and explicit infra swaps (Unity→MS.DI, ConfigurationManager→IOptions) as named deliverables; the others imply modernized internals without all of those specifics. This is an implementation-detail difference inside the shared 'modernize the host/DI/serialization' mandate, not a different task. Net: same task, same surfaces, same observable behavior; divergence is in how completely each enumerates the surrounding preflight pipeline deliverables.
